disease_label_per_paper: Cytokine release syndrome complicated with rhabdomyolysis after chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy
presentation_summary: Relapsed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia with >90% marrow blasts before sequential CD22/CD19/CD22 CAR-T infusion.
Fever began on day 1 after CAR-T infusion and rose to 40.3 C on days 2-3.
On day 8 she developed severe CRS with hypoxemia, hypotension, tachycardia, capillary leak, neurologic symptoms, and rhabdomyolysis.

Treated with methylprednisolone, dexamethasone, tocilizumab, ICU transfer, plasma exchange, blood purification, transfusion, and antimicrobials; recovered and achieved MRD-negative complete remission at 6 weeks.

clinical_timeline.event: Final CD22 CAR-T infusion after CD22 infusion day -2 and CD19 infusion day -1.
Intermittent fever began at night and transiently responded to antipyretics.
Fever rose despite antipyretics; methylprednisolone, dexamethasone and tocilizumab used as CRS therapy.
Severe bilateral lower limb pain developed, later recognized with CK/myoglobin rise as rhabdomyolysis.
Hypoxemia, hypotension, tachycardia, facial swelling, conjunctival hemorrhage, very high IL-6/ferritin and rhabdomyolysis; transferred to ICU and plasma exchange started.
Plasma exchange and blood purification administered simultaneously.
Transferred back to hematology ward from ICU with stable condition.
Complete remission with MRD negativity at 6 weeks after CAR-T therapy.
